pairs.registryProposal: The golden path sets this subject against prompt-assembly, but a product-owned system prompt that the same program assembles and sends on every run of a flow is still the uncuttable brief. Say that case is in scope.

pairs.subject: agent-instruction-files
pairs.evidence: src/features/plugins/fleet/SkillLibraryDrawer.tsx:86 The drawer starts a skill by typing its slash name and offers install-to-repo, and neither path writes a listing tier or a retention decision.

techniques.evidence: src/features/plugins/fleet/FleetHooksPill.tsx:10 This file is header chrome for hook install status, not an always-loaded instruction file.
src/features/plugins/fleet/FleetHooksPill.tsx:32 The pill calls an installer; it does not carry a prose rule to sort into a gate.
src/features/plugins/fleet/SkillLibraryDrawer.tsx:241 The drawer implements install into a repo and has no keep-or-remove review beside it.
src/features/plugins/fleet/SkillLibraryDrawer.tsx:86 A person starts the skill by name, which the technique maps to name-only, and this drawer never writes that tier.

pairs.registryProposal: listing-tier-by-initiator says the installer writes the consumer's listed / name-only / hidden setting. installSkill here takes name, source, target, and overwrite only, so the tier has nowhere to go.
